So neither is 'scene 0'.

Otherwise it requires v1 = [0x80082504] == 6 -- the per-level scene/overlay selector that scene_flow_dispatcher itself loads from the table at 0x80077FA0 + level*4 -- AND [0x800B3FE0] != 0.
HANDOFF_0x80050210_BELONGS_TO_D05_2026-0.0x800B3FE0_has_no_writer: A whole-image scan finds exactly ONE reference to 0x800B3FE0 anywhere in the retail files: this LOAD. No store exists in the resident EXE or in BITS/MEMORY.BIN. The address sits in the overlay window BELOW MEMORY.BIN's base (0x800B5788), so whatever sets it lives in a different overlay -- i.e. this path is gated on state owned by some level/scene overlay.
HANDOFF_0x80050210_BELONGS_TO_D05_2026-0.conclusion: 0x80050210 is a DISTINCT, SCENE-GATED DEATH CLASS: a life consumed through the scene-flow dispatcher rather than through respawn_transition_state_handler, reachable only for the scene whose selector is 6 and when that overlay's global is set. Neither of the two C16 movies took it, which is consistent -- both were ordinary damage deaths in a normal level.
